c.tagline: Georgia's palm-fringed Black Sea resort of casinos, quirky towers and subtropical rain.

taxi.fareNote: Most taxis are unmarked and unmetered — agree the fare before getting in, or use Bolt or Yandex Go for a fixed app price.

emergency.note: 112 is Georgia's unified emergency number for police, ambulance, and fire, with English-speaking operators available.

avoid.reason: Watch for inflated bills at casinos, strip clubs and some seafront bars, plus petty theft on the crowded beach in peak summer.

hood_desc: The historic core around Europe Square and the Piazza, with pastel 19th-century facades, cafes, wine bars and the main sights; best for first-timers who want everything walkable.
The green promenade strip along Batumi Boulevard, lined with beachfront hotels, bike paths, fountains and the Ali & Nino moving statue; central and lively through the summer.
The modern high-rise quarter at the north end of the boulevard, home to the Alphabet Tower, casinos, clubs and towers like the Sheraton and Hilton; the city's nightlife hub.
A quieter seaside village about 12 km south near the Turkish border, with a pebble beach, the Roman-era Gonio fortress and a relaxed, family-friendly feel.
A calm coastal suburb just north of the center reached by the Argo cable car and marshrutka, with a quieter beach and lower prices; good for a slower base.

water.note: Tap water is generally safe to drink, though many visitors prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Municipal buses run roughly 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM; the Argo cable car operates daytime into the evening (around 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM in summer).
transit.note: Batumi has no metro or tram; a modern municipal bus network plus marshrutka minibuses cover the city, and the Argo cable car links the seafront to the Anuria hilltop. Bolt and Yandex Go fill late-night gaps.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid with the BatumiCard or a contactless bank card on board (around 0.50 GEL); marshrutkas take cash. The cable car has a separate ticket (around 15-20 GEL round trip).

bus: Intercity marshrutkas and buses to Tbilisi, Kutaisi and Turkey
ferry: Batumi Sea Port (cargo, with occasional passenger and cruise calls)
train: Georgian Railway: Batumi-Tbilisi line from Batumi Central, plus summer trains toward Kutaisi and Zugdidi

transit.m: City bus #10 to the center (~20 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving ~10% for good service is appreciated. Some restaurants already add a service charge to the bill.

food.name: Acharuli khachapuri
food.desc: The boat-shaped bread of Adjara, filled with molten cheese, crowned with a raw yolk and butter, then stirred together and torn apart by hand.

places.name: Laguna
places.note: Basement cafe open since 1997; the local benchmark for Adjarian khachapuri.

places.name: Retro
places.note: Ranked among the world's best by TasteAtlas, with an unusually wide range of fillings.

places.name: Porto Franco
places.note: Holds the top TasteAtlas rating for Adjarian khachapuri worldwide.

food.name: Borano
food.desc: Adjara's mountain dish of fresh sulguni melted slowly in clarified butter until it pulls into ropes. Eaten straight from the pan with bread.

places.name: BatuMarani
places.note: Nine tenths of the menu is Adjarian, built on family recipes from villages around the city.

places.name: Cafe Adjara
places.note: Its lunch set puts six small Adjarian dishes on one tray, borano included.

places.name: Adjarian Wine House
places.note: Valley estate an hour inland; mountain cooking with its own vineyards.

food.name: Sinori
food.desc: Strips of thin bread layered with sour cream and salty nadughi curd, rolled up and warmed. A rich, little-exported Adjarian speciality.

places.name: Cafe Adjara
places.note: One of the few places that reliably serves sinori, on its Adjarian tasting set.

places.name: BatuMarani
places.note: Village-recipe kitchen that keeps the rarer Adjarian dishes on the menu.

places.name: Keda valley guesthouses
places.note: Family tables in the mountains where sinori is still everyday food.

food.name: Achma
food.desc: Layer upon layer of boiled pasta sheets and cheese baked into a soft, buttery slab - the lasagne-like cousin of khachapuri.

places.name: Retro
places.note: Wide khachapuri family menu, achma included, in a busy central room.

places.name: BatuMarani
places.note: Traditional achma cut into thick squares, best shared.

places.name: Old Town bakeries
places.note: Neighbourhood bakeries sell achma by the slice through the morning.

food.name: Malakhto
food.desc: A cold Adjarian paste of crushed beans with walnut, coriander and blue fenugreek, scooped up with mchadi corn bread.

places.name: Cafe Adjara
places.note: Part of the six-dish Adjarian lunch set that makes this the easiest tasting in town.

places.name: BatuMarani
places.note: Served as part of a spread of cold village starters.

places.name: Batumi Central Market
places.note: Market cooks sell malakhto and bean dishes to take away by weight.

food.name: Fried Black Sea fish
food.desc: Barabulka mullet and small kefali dusted in cornmeal and fried crisp, eaten whole with lemon and a pile of raw onion. Cheap and seasonal.

places.name: Batumi Fish Market
places.note: Buy your fish by the kilo downstairs, hand it upstairs and they fry it while you wait.

places.name: Laguna
places.note: Long-running local cafe that does the fried fish plate well.

places.name: Boulevard seafront cafes
places.note: Beachside kitchens along the promenade frying the day's catch.

food.name: Chacha
food.desc: Georgian grape pomace spirit, fierce and clear, distilled at home across Adjara. Toasted in small glasses with a supra-style speech.

places.name: Batumi Central Market
places.note: Stallholders sell homemade chacha and let you taste before you buy.

places.name: Adjarian Wine House
places.note: Estate tastings pair its chacha with mountain cheese and bread.

places.name: Old Town wine bars
places.note: Small bars around Piazza pour chacha flights alongside Georgian wine.

food.name: Qvevri wine
food.desc: Wine fermented in buried clay eggs, a UNESCO-listed method. Adjara's own Chkhaveri grape makes a pale, delicate rose-tinted red.

places.name: Adjarian Wine House
places.note: Working winery in the Acharistskali valley focused on native Adjarian grapes.

places.name: BatuMarani
places.note: Marani means wine cellar; the list leans hard on Georgian qvevri bottles.

places.name: Old Town wine bars
places.note: Cluster of tasting rooms pouring amber and qvevri wines by the glass.

landmarks: Batumi Boulevard
A seven-kilometer seaside park of palms, fountains, and beach bars tracing the pebbled Black Sea shore since 1881.
Ali and Nino Statue
Two eight-meter steel figures glide toward each other, merge, and pass through one another nightly, embodying a tragic Caucasus love story.
Batumi Botanical Garden
One of the world's great coastal gardens, terraced over green cliffs at Mtsvane Kontskhi with flora from nine climate zones.
Alphabet Tower
A 130-meter DNA-helix tower spiraled with the 33 letters of the Georgian script, celebrating the nation's unique alphabet.
Piazza Batumi
An Italian-style square of mosaics, stained glass, and campanile, hosting open-air concerts in the heart of the old town.
Europe Square and the Medea Statue
A grand square of Belle Époque facades centered on golden-fleeced Medea, linking Batumi to the myth of Colchis.
Argo Cable Car and Anuria Hill
A 2.5-kilometer cable car gliding above rooftops to a hilltop terrace with the definitive panorama of Batumi's bay and skyline.
Gonio Fortress
A remarkably intact Roman-Byzantine fortress south of the city, linked to legends of the Argonauts and the Apostle Matthias's grave.
Dancing Fountains of Lake Ardagani
Summer evenings erupt in choreographed jets, lasers, and music over the boulevard's lake, a beloved free nightly spectacle.
Orta Jame Mosque and Old Batumi
The 19th-century mosque at the heart of Batumi's atmospheric old quarter, amid cafés, courtyards, and Ottoman-era architecture.

intl.to: Yerevan (Armenia) - summer-season overnight service via Tbilisi

train.note: Batumi's mainline terminus is Batumi Central at Makhinjauri, about 5 km north of the seafront, linked to the centre by minibus and taxi - do not expect to walk in. Stadler double-deck expresses cover Tbilisi in around five hours with several departures a day, plus slower overnight trains added in summer. The through sleeper from Yerevan runs only during the summer timetable and has been suspended in some years, so confirm with Georgian Railway before building a trip around it; Armenian border formalities are done on the train. Tickets go on sale online and at the station a few weeks ahead and the summer expresses sell out, especially at weekends.

intl.to: Trabzon, Rize & Hopa (Turkey) - via the Sarpi border 20 km south, 4-6 hr
Istanbul, Ankara, Izmir & Antalya (Turkey) - long-distance overnight coaches

bus.note: International coaches and marshrutkas leave from the Batumi bus station and from operator offices near the old town, and Turkish companies dominate the traffic south. Sarpi, 20 km down the coast, is a 24-hour crossing where everyone gets off the vehicle for passport control; most EU, UK, US and Georgian nationals enter Turkey visa-free or with an e-visa bought online in advance. Trabzon is 4-6 hours depending on the queue, Istanbul an 18-20 hour overnight haul. Domestically, marshrutkas run to Tbilisi in about 6 hours and to Kutaisi in 2, leaving when full from the bus station; pay the driver in cash.

ferry.note: Batumi's port handles containers, oil and seasonal cruise calls but has no scheduled passenger ferry. The Ro-Pax link across the Black Sea to Chornomorsk near Odesa has not operated since 2022, and the Turkish port of Trabzon and Georgian-administered Sukhumi are both closed to passenger sailings, so the only boats you can board in Batumi are short pleasure cruises along the seafront.

half.name: Makhuntseti Waterfall & Machakhela National Park
half.blurb: A waterfall and old stone arch bridge in the forested Adjara hills, gateway to Machakhela National Park's mountain villages.

half.name: Kobuleti
half.blurb: A quieter seaside town north of Batumi with a long pebble beach and a protected wetland reserve behind the shore.

half.name: Mtirala National Park
half.blurb: A rainforest park in the Adjara mountains with hiking trails, waterfalls, and some of the highest rainfall totals in the Caucasus.

full.name: Martvili Canyon
full.blurb: A turquoise river gorge in Samegrelo where boats and a short hike lead past waterfalls and pools carved into limestone cliffs.

full.name: Okatse Canyon
full.blurb: A steep limestone canyon with a suspended metal walkway bolted to the cliff face above a rushing river.
